clue.text: In the sun, but not hatched

blocks.note: first meaning: out in full sunlight, with no shelter overhead
second meaning: in drawing, hatching is shading done with fine parallel lines

explanation.surface: A chick basking in the sunshine that has not yet broken out of its egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hatched' pretends to be about eggs; it is the artist's word for shading with lines.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means lacking shade, which fits both sunlit ground and a drawing left without any pencilled shading lines.

clue.text: In the saddle, goes hard and has a spill

blocks.note: a rider who is mounted is up
concrete or jelly sets when it goes hard

explanation.surface: A jockey rides hard and then falls off.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset something is to knock it over, so whoever upsets a cup or vessel causes a spill.

clue.text: How the movements of the arms can give away information

definitions.text: How the movements of the arms can give away information

blocks.clueFragment: How the movements of the arms can give away information
blocks.note: surface reading: careless gestures or body language betraying a secret
setter's reading: deliberate arm positions spelling out a message by a recognised code

explanation.surface: Someone's gestures betray what they are trying to hide.
explanation.definitionFit: Semaphore signals letters by holding two flags in set positions, so the signaller's limbs transmit messages.

clue.text: A great friend married Ernie as an example

blocks.note: taken as written
a crony is a close friend
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: Someone's best mate married a man called Ernie.
explanation.walkthrough: ERNIE is the machine that picks Premium Bond winners in Britain: Electronic Random Number Indicator Equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: An acronym is a word formed from initial letters, and ERNIE is a well-known British instance.

clue.text: English team on the way to survive

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a cricket or football side has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: An English side travelling to a match just needs to hang on.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to live or carry on being, close to keeping alive.

clue.text: Opening for toe on a slipper has charm

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its very first letter, so only the start of the next word is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
a mule is a backless slipper
first letter of toe

explanation.surface: A slipper with an open toe is said to have its own appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' in an across clue puts the letter from toe after the slipper.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucky charm is a small object worn to ward off harm, which is exactly what an amulet is.

clue.text: Perhaps our men on the river are keener

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters given are only one possible order of the word wanted

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Our rowers out on the river may be the more enthusiastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keener' reads as 'more eager'; it is a noun, one who keens, wailing for the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to wail in grief at a funeral, so a keener is someone lamenting the dead.

clue.text: On the king, material with gold thread is not very effective

blocks.note: lamé is fabric woven with metallic thread
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king's gold-threaded robes are rather useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' in a down clue puts the fabric above the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Lame means weak or unconvincing, so a lamer excuse or effort is one that works less well.

clue.text: Try a lone trip of a mountainous area

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so the letters fall over into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to go on a solo journey into the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyrol is an Alpine region of Austria and Italy, and Tyrolean describes things from there.

clue.text: Obscure coteries

indicators.note: to obscure something is to disguise it, so the letters are hidden in another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' works twice: as the definition and as the instruction to disguise the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by a small inner circle, so it is little known.

clue.text: The way an adder traps birds when it's warm in autumn

definitions.note: a clause standing for a noun: a warm spell late in the year

indicators.note: to trap something is to hold it inside, so the birds sit within the other letters

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
one who sums, or adds up, is a summer
martins are swallow-like birds

explanation.surface: A snake catching birds when the weather turns warm late in the year.
explanation.walkthrough: The adder is not a snake but someone who adds up; the street abbreviation and that word are split so the birds sit between them.
explanation.definitionFit: St Martin's summer is a spell of mild weather around Martinmas, 11 November, an autumn warm spell like an Indian summer.

clue.text: Superior group at the Turk's Head

definitions.note: a cryptic phrase: what sits at the top of a Turk's head

blocks.note: top means highest or best
a knot is a small cluster of people

explanation.surface: The best crowd drinking at a pub called the Turk's Head.
explanation.walkthrough: The Turk's Head looks like a pub sign, and is also the name of a knot; read literally it is a man's head, where a topknot is worn.
explanation.definitionFit: A topknot is hair tied up in a bunch on the crown, so it is found at the top of someone's head.

clue.text: Twister gets tax-free return by endless practice

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so the letters are read from the end
something without an end has lost its final letter

blocks.note: a net figure is what is left after tax
drill is repeated practice

explanation.surface: A con man secures a tax-free profit thanks to relentless rehearsal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is the thin coiling shoot a climbing plant winds around supports, so it twists.

clue.text: It helps to get tight in a private saloon

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a tool

blocks.note: Tommy is slang for a British private soldier
a saloon bar is a room in a British pub

explanation.surface: A soldier gets drunk in a pub's saloon bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' suggests drunk, but here it means fastened firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: A tommy bar is a short rod pushed through a box spanner for leverage when tightening nuts.

clue.text: Hector our of position? Start the game!

blocks.note: to hector someone is to bully them
off means out of position, as in off target

explanation.surface: Someone named Hector is out of place, and the match is about to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our' is a newspaper misprint for 'out'. Hector looks like a name but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A bully-off was the old way of starting a hockey match, two players clashing sticks over the ball.

clue.text: Continental agreement on port wine from Spain

indicators.note: in an across clue, being on something means following it, so the agreement is written after the port

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro is a port
ja is yes in German, a European agreement

explanation.surface: Europeans reach a deal on port and on Spanish wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' in an across clue puts the yes after the port; 'port' looks like the drink but is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red wine made in the La Rioja region of northern Spain.

clue.text: Fringes for old-fashioned garments

blocks.note: first meaning: the outer edges of a town
second meaning read in two parts: 'out' means unfashionable, and skirts are garments

explanation.surface: Decorative trimming on outdated clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: The edge districts of a city are its outer parts, and dated skirts would be 'out' skirts.

clue.text: Promising to become attractive

blocks.note: first meaning: pledging to marry, getting betrothed
second meaning: charming and pleasant

explanation.surface: A person showing signs of growing more appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage is to pledge oneself to marry; as an adjective the word means charming and winning.

clue.text: Kinswoman found in resort without English

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the resort wraps around the other letter

blocks.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A female relative turns up on holiday where no English is spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a female relative, the daughter of a brother or sister.

clue.text: Eeyore's ghastly sight

indicators.note: ghastly suggests something horribly disfigured, so the word is pulled out of shape

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: The gloomy donkey from Winnie-the-Pooh looks dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: A sight in the colloquial sense is something ugly, as in 'you look a sight', which is an unsightly object.

clue.text: Get cut, mixing ale out of crate perhaps

indicators.note: mixing stirs things together, so the letters that follow are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gets hurt rummaging ale bottles out of a crate.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to tear or gash flesh, a ragged kind of wound.

clue.text: Woman with no capital married and began again

indicators.note: a capital is a word's first letter, and having none means the opening letter goes

blocks.note: Irene is a woman's name
wed means married

explanation.surface: A penniless woman got married and made a fresh start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No capital' suggests no money; it means losing the initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew something is to resume it after a break, so renewed works as started over.

clue.text: Russian port does as a cocktail

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixed drink, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A port city behaves like a mixed drink.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1994 setters still called the Black Sea city Russian; it is in Ukraine.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Black Sea port, formerly part of the Russian Empire and the Soviet Union.

clue.text: The school of a chartered accountant and Oxford scholar

blocks.note: taken as written
CA is the abbreviation for chartered accountant
a demy is a scholar of Magdalen College, Oxford

explanation.surface: The college that produced an accountant and an Oxford academic.
explanation.definitionFit: An academy is a school or place of learning, often a specialised one.

clue.text: Noisy woman helper

indicators.note: noisy means making sound, so the name is judged by how it is spoken

blocks.note: Aida is the heroine of Verdi's opera

explanation.surface: A loud-mouthed female assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: One who aids gives assistance, so the word names somebody offering support.

clue.text: Kind son somehow preventing one from slipping

indicators.note: somehow means by some unknown means, so the letters arrive in an unstated order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A caring boy stops someone from losing their footing.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-skid surfaces or tyres are designed to grip, keeping a person or vehicle from sliding.

clue.text: Small county to dismiss workers — it's a direction

indicators.note: dismissing staff sends them away, so these letters are removed

blocks.note: Northants is the short name for Northamptonshire, an English county
worker ants are the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: A small English county lays off its staff and points the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' signals the abbreviated name of the county, not a tiny one.
explanation.definitionFit: North is one of the four cardinal points of the compass.

clue.text: Sparklers, say, causing domestic rows

blocks.note: first meaning: small pyrotechnics safe to set off inside a house
second meaning: figurative explosions of temper at home

explanation.surface: Lighting sparklers in the house leads to family arguments.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is literal for small pyrotechnics used inside, and figurative for heated quarrels within a household.

clue.text: Fish catch --- a stone

blocks.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
to net is to catch

explanation.surface: An angler's haul is merely a rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Garnet is a deep red gemstone, a silicate mineral used in jewellery.

clue.text: Greek island - one with a colony in Africa once

blocks.note: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Dodecanese
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Greek island linked to a former African colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodesia was the British colony in southern Africa named after Cecil Rhodes, now Zimbabwe and Zambia.
